title: [28/2/2024] Population figures for four countries 2003-2050
prompt: The table below shows population figures for four countries for 2003 and projected figures for 2025 and 2050. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make a comparison where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the actual and projected population figures, measured in millions, for four different countries over three specific years: 2003, 2025 and 2050.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, except for Italy, which is expected to see a steady decline in its population, all other countries are forecast to experience growth during the period shown. Among the four nations, Indonesia had the highest population in 2003 and is projected to maintain this position through to 2050.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the countries with continuous population growth, in 2003, Indonesia's figure of 238 million was significantly higher than that of Argentina, at just 34 million. The population of Argentina is forecast to almost double by 2050, reaching 62 million, while Indonesia's numbers are predicted to rise by nearly one-third to 312 million.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining nations, Italy and the Republic of Korea had relatively similar populations in 2003, at 54 and 48 million respectively. However, Italy's population is expected to fall consistently to 45 million by 2050, while Korea's numbers are projected to increase slightly to 52 million by 2025 and then stabilize at this level until 2050.
